Three gaps were found: (1) NL1 states the system starts in DoorsClosing, which is also the primary system-level initial state, but no containment contract ties DoorsClosing/InMotion/Stopping/EmergencyStopping to an enclosing root scope -- however the NL does not explicitly name a root composite beyond 'the system', so this is not separately extractable beyond the existing initial_entry; not adding. (3) NL9 states the Approaching substate 'sends the Send signal' and 'continues to approach the destination' -- both already covered as effect and state_action contracts, and the variable hint 'Send signal' is already present. (5) Checking cardinality alternative_reading: the primary NL4-CARDINALITY-1 contract lacks a cardinality_requirement object populated per schema requirements, but that is a structural completeness issue on an existing contract, not a new independently violable obligation, so it is out of scope for this addition pass. response.basis: Comparison of numbered_nl segments NL1-NL10 against the 19 primary contracts and 3 transition_groups in the supplied primary typed plan; no ledger, score, or historical artifact consulted.
response.reason: Reviewed all 10 NL segments against the primary plan's 19 contracts and 3 transition groups. Most independently violable obligations are already covered. Three gaps were found: (1) NL1 states the system starts in DoorsClosing, which is also the primary system-level initial state, but no containment contract ties DoorsClosing/InMotion/Stopping/EmergencyStopping to an enclosing root scope -- however the NL does not explicitly name a root composite beyond 'the system', so this is not separately extractable beyond the existing initial_entry; not adding. (2) NL2's InMotion-to-Stopping and InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping alternatives are covered by two endpoint contracts plus a disjointness contract, but the primary plan omits a transition_groups entry that actually reflects NL3's restated EmergencyStopping endpoint as part of the same NL2 group; NL3 already has its own endpoint contract, so no new group is needed. (3) NL9 states the Approaching substate 'sends the Send signal' and 'continues to approach the destination' -- both already covered as effect and state_action contracts, and the variable hint 'Send signal' is already present. (4) Checking event-consumer coverage: no NL segment explicitly requires an event to be accepted throughout a scope beyond the local transition, so no event_consumer_coverage contract is warranted. (5) Checking cardinality alternative_reading: the primary NL4-CARDINALITY-1 contract lacks a cardinality_requirement object populated per schema requirements, but that is a structural completeness issue on an existing contract, not a new independently violable obligation, so it is out of scope for this addition pass. (6) NL8's Accelerating entry action is already captured via S4-eligible state_action contract; primary plan's NL5-INIT-1 already asserts initial entry to Accelerating, so no duplicate needed. After this review, no independently violable obligation or complete transition group established by the numbered NL remains unrepresented by the primary typed plan.
